title: prefill-decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage overlap + kernel scheduler improvements
author: Leah Patel
release_notes: Optimizes prefill/decode pipeline: chunked prefill for long-context batches, speculative prefill path to warm KV cache, stage-overlap scheduling and kernel prioritization. Reduces p95/p99 latency and increases throughput for mixed prefill+decode workloads. No API changes.
description: Motivation: Long-context prefill workloads and mixed prefill+decode traffic expose inefficiencies in our pipeline: large contiguous prefill requests block decode work, KV cache warmup is suboptimal for interactive workloads, and kernel selection doesn't prioritize short-latency decode kernels. This PR implements three complementary optimizations: 1) chunked prefill: split very long prefill requests into smaller chunks that can be scheduled independently so we can interleave decode work and reduce head-of-line blocking; 2) speculative prefill: opportunistically run a lightweight prefill pass for active sessions to warm the KV cache ahead of full prefill where we detect likely continuation (heuristic-based with opt-out); 3) stage overlap + kernel scheduler: allow the prefill and decode stages to overlap on the same device when safe, and introduce a kernel scheduler that prioritizes low-latency decode kernels while still keeping throughput for bulk prefill. Implementation summary/notes: - Added runtime/prefill/prefill_chunker.cpp and prefill_chunker.h: chunking logic, configurable chunk sizes, and backpressure hooks. - Added runtime/prefill/speculative_prefill.cpp: speculative path that is gated behind a feature flag and respects per-customer opt-out, with telemetry hooks for hit/miss. - Modified runtime/scheduler/kernel_scheduler.cpp: new prioritization queues and lightweight preemption for single-GPU workloads. - Modified runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager.cpp: support for speculative entries and TTL tuning to avoid thrashing. - Adjusted runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cpp to be aware of chunk boundaries and to prevent large prefill groups from monopolizing batch windows. - Added tests: tests/perf/prefill_decode_bench.py and unit tests under tests/unit/prefill/* to exercise chunking/speculative paths. - Added docs/perf/prefill_decode.md with benchmarks and tuning recommendations. Backwards compatibility and safety: all new behaviors are behind a runtime feature flag or gated per-tenant. Defaults keep current behavior for existing deployments. Extensive unit and e2e tests added to guard correctness. Benchmarks: - Mixed interactive workload (50% prefill long-context, 50% short decode): throughput +18% median tokens/sec, p95 latency -18% relative, p99 -34%. - Long-context prefill batch (single large prefill requests): throughput +28% when chunking enabled due to better GPU utilization. - KV-hit rate for interactive sessions improved from ~62% to ~85% under speculative prefill in our CI harness. See docs/perf/prefill_decode.md for full graphs and configs. Checklist: - [x] Chunked prefill implementation and unit tests - [x] Speculative prefill feature with telemetry - [x] Kernel scheduler + stage overlap implementation - [x] E2E perf benchmarks and CI perf checks - [x] Docs and runtime feature flag - [x] No API-breaking changes Related: ENG-4721 (prefill memory growth investigation), INT-761 (customer incident that motivated aggressive KV warming).
commits: squash: implement chunked prefill; add speculative prefill path; introduce kernel scheduler and stage overlap; kv cache speculative entries; make continuous batcher chunk-aware; add perf tests and docs; fix race on scheduler handoff (follow-up commit)
discussion:
Miguel Torres: Found a race where the scheduler handoff could try to preempt a kernel mid-copy; requested explicit handoff handshake.
Leah Patel: Added a handshake and updated kernel_scheduler tests to cover the path; also added a small delay in the continuous_batcher integration test to reproduce locally.
Anita Gomez: Please add a test that validates speculative prefill doesn't double-count tokens for billing.
Leah Patel: Added telemetry counter and unit test; speculative path reports 'speculative_tokens' separately and does not affect billable token counters.
Daniel Park: Verified perf numbers on our perf-lab (A100) and approved once CI flakiness was addressed.
CI: initial perf job flagged a flaky scheduler handoff test; re-run after handshake fix and all checks passed. Approvals: Miguel Torres (LGTM), Anita Gomez (LGTM), Daniel Park (approved).
